issue.title: Restrict Athena Prometheus, pushgateway, and node-exporter listeners to intended clients
issue.description: Inventory legitimate Prometheus scrapes, push clients, dashboards and existing firewall policy. Choose loopback/tailnet-bound listeners or an equivalent restricted access path that preserves required clients; apply through reviewed sase_sudo and verify both allowed access and denied unintended access. Do not blindly bind every service to loopback before checking remote clients. Keep the bob-cli-8v email route and apt-health scrape working. Distinct from bob-cli-8r detection rules and bob-cli-8u supervisor RPC exposure. Size large because the intended access boundary and remote consumers require planning.

task_type_fields.impact: Monitoring data and the pushgateway ingestion surface are exposed to every network interface allowed by the host firewall, beyond a deliberately chosen monitoring audience.
task_type_fields.repro: On athena at 2026-10-18 landing, ss -ltn shows LISTEN *:9090, *:9091 and *:9100, while Alertmanager is 127.0.0.1:9093. This confirms wildcard binds, not public-internet reachability; firewall and network routes still need inspection.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by bob-cli-8v.1 note #4 and confirmed during landing; these pre-existing wildcard listeners expose monitoring endpoints beyond the new loopback-only Alertmanager.

payload.description: Restrict monitoring listeners without disrupting future detection rules or the existing email route
Adjacent pre-existing network exposures on Athena, with separate services and fixes
